learn.title: From words to an equation
learn.body: Word problems are equations in disguise. Name the unknown with a letter, turn each phrase into maths, solve, then check the answer against the story, not just the equation.

learn.title: A gym fee problem
learn.body: A gym charges 20 dollars to join plus 15 dollars per month. Your total is 110 dollars. How many months?
steps: Let $m$ be the number of months

learn.title: Consecutive integers
learn.body: Two consecutive integers add up to 41. Find them.
steps: Let the first be $n$, so the next is $n+1$

learn.title: Useful phrases
learn.body: Sum means add. Difference means subtract. Product means multiply. Twice means $2x$. Per means each, so it multiplies. Is or equals becomes the equals sign.
After solving, ask if the answer makes sense. A number of months or tickets should not be negative or a fraction.

questions.prompt: Which equation says: three times a number, minus 4, is 11?
questions.explanation: Three times the number is $3x$. Then subtract 4, giving $3x-4=11$.

questions.prompt: Twice a number plus 6 equals 20. What is the number?
Popcorn costs 6 dollars. Tickets cost 8 dollars each. The total is 38 dollars. How many tickets?
A taxi charges 3 dollars plus 2 dollars per km. The fare is 17 dollars. Which equation fits?
questions.explanation: The fixed 3 dollars is added once, and 2 dollars is paid for each of the $k$ kilometres.

questions.prompt: Three consecutive integers add up to 48. What is the smallest?
Ana is 4 years older than Ben. Together they are 30. How old is Ben?
